main_text.p: ut judicet nos, quibus ex mandato Dei suffragatur Samuel, iisque pariter effrenè futuri Regis his verbis graphicè depingit ingenium,{c} Agros vestros, & vineas, & oliveta tollet, & dabit servis suis, servos etiam vestros & ancillas, & juvenes optimos, & asinos auferet, & ponet in opere suo [quasi dixisset:] haec facturus est, non tam quod ei facere liceat, (aliter enim describitur Regis officium, Deut.1 7:) sed quod ei talia molienti, vobis resistere non liceat. Quare non subnectit, vi ejus jugum excutietis, aut à solio deturbabitis, aut per insidias interficietis, aut auferetis eum veneno: sed{d} clamabitis in die illa à facie Regis vestri quem elegistis vobis.Nam ut prudenter & christianè{e} Tacitus: bonos Principes voto expetere debemus, qualescunque pati, & quomodo sterilitatem, aut nimios imbres, & cetera naturae mala, sic luxum & avaritiam dominantium tolerare. Rationem ipse alibi reddit,{f} Principi summum rerum judicium Dij dederunt, subditis obsequij gloria relicta est: &{g} nihil tam exasperat fervorem vulneris, quam ferendi impatientia.Populus itaque cùm verf.14.verf.18.Histor.4.Aunal.4.[?]Egesip.l.2.

page.notes: Marginal references are read as printed; "Aunal.4." may be a misprint for "Annal.4." and is marked [?]. The section mark before "nihil" is printed like a letter g and is read as the mark {g}. The reference "Deut.1 7:)" is printed with a space. The text runs on through the whole column as one paragraph, with no indent on any line. The last line "ob" is the catchword.
